sections.label: Active Mobility Bill powers
sections.summary: The Government accepted the panel's recommendations in full, and the Active Mobility Bill seeks to grant LTA powers to implement them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Government had accepted the panel's recommendations in full, and the Active Mobility Bill now seeks to grant the Land Transport Authority (LTA) the powers to implement them.

sections.label: Footpath speed limit rules
sections.summary: Regulations will specify that bicycles and PMDs allowed on footpaths must travel below 15 km/h.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The regulations will specify that bicycles and PMDs, which are allowed on footpaths, must travel below 15 kilometres per hour (km/h), similar to an average person's running speed.

sections.label: Shared paths speed limit
sections.summary: Bicycles, PMDs and PABs will be allowed on shared paths, with a speed limit of 25 km/h.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We will allow bicycles, PMDs and PABs on these shared paths.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We will also permit a slightly higher speed limit of 25 km/h.

sections.label: Penalties for flouting rules
sections.summary: A person who flouts these rules will be liable upon conviction to a fine not exceeding $1,000, or imprisonment not exceeding three months, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: A person who flouts these rules will be liable upon conviction to a fine not exceeding $1,000, or to imprisonment not exceeding three months, or both.

sections.label: Offences and penalties clauses
sections.summary: Clauses 19, 21, 22 and 23 set penalties for non-compliant devices, other contraventions, and failing to stop and render assistance in an accident.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clause 19 of the Bill prohibits the use of non-compliant devices on public paths.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Those who contravene this rule will be liable upon conviction to a fine not exceeding $5,000, or to imprisonment not exceeding three months, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Clauses 21 and 22 impose steep penalties upon conviction, which include a fine not exceeding $5,000, or imprisonment not exceeding six months, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In addition, clause 23 makes it an offence if a cyclist, PMD user or PAB rider does not stop to render assistance in an accident.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Those found contravening this rule will be liable upon conviction to a fine not exceeding $3,000 or to imprisonment not exceeding 12 months, or both.

sections.label: Road Traffic Act amendments
sections.summary: The Road Traffic Act will be amended to prohibit PMDs on public roads, and subsidiary legislation will mandate registration of PABs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Road Traffic Act will be amended to prohibit the use of PMDs on public roads, for the safety of the riders and other motorists.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Transport (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We will also be making amendments to the subsidiary legislation under the Road Traffic Act to mandate the registration of PABs, which are more prone to illegal modification and have a greater potential to cause serious injury.

sections.label: Active Mobility Bill regulating PMDs
sections.summary: The Active Mobility Bill seeks to regulate the use of PMDs, which the passage calls imperative.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The Active Mobility Bill seeks to regulate the use of PMDs and it is imperative that this is done.

sections.label: Mandatory minimum age for PMDs
sections.summary: The passage asks whether a mandatory minimum age for the use of PMDs can be considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Can we consider imposing a mandatory minimum age for the use of PMDs?

sections.label: Third-party insurance for PMD users
sections.summary: The passage notes motor accident protection, asks about mandating third-party insurance for PMD users, and cites Mrs Josephine Teo's 2016 reply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: This offers consolation and financial protection to families, especially when it is the breadwinners who are involved in an unfortunate and tragic motor accident.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: We do not have similar protection for accident victims involving PMDs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: On this issue, several Members of this House, myself included, have asked if a similar form of third-party insurance could be mandated for PMD users.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Senior Minister of State Mrs Josephine Teo had in her oral reply in Parliament on 10 October 2016 replied that it will be "too onerous and costly for the vast majority of cyclists and PMD users who behave responsibly and safely".

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: She further added that "pedestrians in Singapore who are injured in accidents can obtain compensation by initiating civil lawsuits or through private settlements".

sections.label: Compensation scheme for PMD accident victims
sections.summary: The passage argues effort and cost should not impede a compensation scheme for PMD accident victims, suggesting a fund like the MIB.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: As such, I am of the humble and respectful view that effort and cost should not be the impediments for the provision of a compensation scheme for PMD accident victims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Indeed, if the provision of third-party insurance is too onerous and costly on PMD users, perhaps a fund, not unlike how the Motor Insurers' Bureau of Singapore (MIB) deals with motor vehicles, could be set up to compensate victims who have no recourse to seek the compensation they need.

sections.label: Easier reporting of accidents
sections.summary: The passage states accidents happen and more can and should be done to ease victim reporting and let Police apprehend culprits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Unfortunately, accidents do happen and more can and should be done to make it easier for victims to report and also allow the Police to apprehend and punish the culprits.

sections.label: Compiling PMD accident data
sections.summary: The passage says the Ministry does not compile accidents involving such equipment except on roads, and urges public education and data tracking.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Currently, the Ministry does not compile the number and nature of accidents involving such equipment which occur on pavements and elsewhere, except those that occur on the roads.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We should educate the public that with this Bill, such reports can and should be made at Police stations, as users of PMDs are legally bound to assist victims and report any accidents.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Such data will allow the Government to keep track of accident patterns and provide useful information on how to improve upon regulations and road designs.

sections.label: LTA enforcement of shared paths
sections.summary: Asks how LTA will monitor and enforce proper shared path use by PMD users after the Bill is enacted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: How will LTA continue to monitor and enforce the proper use of shared paths by PMD users after the Bill is officially enacted?

sections.label: Shared path width and gradient guidelines
sections.summary: Asks whether LTA would stipulate guidelines on minimum width and maximum gradient of shared paths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Would LTA stipulate guidelines on the minimum width and maximum gradient of shared paths?

sections.label: Safety course for PAB users
sections.summary: Asks whether LTA would mandate a basic safety course before PAB users register their PABs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For their personal safety, would LTA consider mandating PAB users to undergo a basic safety course as a prerequisite to registering their PABs?

sections.label: Insurance or compensation for accident victims
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry will consider mandatory insurance for PMD and PAB users or a compensation framework for accident victims.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: She had to undergo two major operations, a lengthy hospital stay and hefty medical bills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I think besides the option of launching into a civil suit against the PMD user, which can pose an additional financial strain on the injured party, will the Ministry look into mandatory insurance coverage for PMD/PAB users or establishing a structured compensation framework for such accident victims?

sections.label: E-scooter monthly sales reported
sections.summary: States that in November 2016 The Straits Times reported monthly e-scooter sales reaching 400.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In November 2016, The Straits Times reported monthly sales of e-scooters hitting 400.

sections.label: Bill, enforcement and footpath regimes
sections.summary: Says the Bill shows intent to reset safety parameters, and notes enforcement and different regimes for footpaths, park connectors and e-bikes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It will depend on the resolve of the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This Bill signifies an intention on the part of the Government to reset the safety parameters and promote a safe cycling culture, in light of new mobility devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I note the severe punishments imposed for various breaches and I am in support as I feel that people have to understand the importance of riding safely and being considerate to other road users.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It will be down to the consistent enforcement efforts of LTA to make the new regulations work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I understand that the Government is going to create different regimes for different footpaths, some can be used by bicycles and e-scooters, some only for pedestrians, and e-bikes will not be allowed on footpaths but will now be allowed on park connectors, although I have seen e-bikes on footpaths and park connectors for many years.

sections.label: Road safety syllabus and throttle
sections.summary: Asks whether the Road Safety Park syllabus and Safe Cycling Programme will cover e-scooters, PMDs and e-bikes, and whether throttle use will be allowed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Will the Government consider upgrading the syllabus of the Road Safety Park to include lessons incorporating new mobility devices covered in this Bill, particularly e-scooters, PMDs and e-bikes?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Will our Safe Cycling Programme, which is being introduced, be incorporated into our school syllabus like in New South Wales, Australia, where they have incorporated road safety programmes into their primary and secondary school syllabus?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I have said that control of speed by throttle is more precise and as long as the maximum speed of the bike is limited, the throttle does not make the bike unsafe.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, is the Government going to allow the use of throttle?

sections.label: Legislation for PMD users and retailers
sections.summary: States that legislation is needed to list appropriate PMD user behaviours and rules for retailers selling or modifying PMDs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: If this is to be successful, we need legislation to list down what are the appropriate behaviours of PMD users and the rules by which retailers must abide by when selling or modifying PMDs .

sections.label: Unlawful PMD behaviours listed
sections.summary: The Bill lists unlawful PMD behaviours such as using a PAB as an e-scooter and illegal modifications that could jeopardise others' safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Bill has listed down unlawful behaviours of PMD users, such as using a PAB as an e-scooter and illegal modifications, which could jeopardise the safety of others.

sections.label: Foldable bikes and PMDs on transport
sections.summary: States that since last month foldable bikes and other PMDs can be taken into MRT trains and buses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Starting from last month, foldable bikes and other PMDs can be taken into MRT trains and buses.

sections.label: Online learning and test benefit
sections.summary: States that although they currently need no driving test, attending online learning and a test would benefit them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Although currently, the latter do not need to pass any driving test, it will be beneficial for them if they could attend online learning and test.

sections.label: Support for the Bill
sections.summary: Supports the Bill while asking whether its purposes are compatible, realistic in a land-scarce city-state and achievable without major public transport infrastructure revamp.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By embracing the needs of a whole range of road users and its vision of promoting healthy and environmentally-friendly alternatives for road usage, allowing connectivity to the public transport network and gradually reducing our heavy dependence on motor vehicles, I strongly support this Bill, although I feel that there are certain aspects of it that require a clearer thought about.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Supporting developments that promote cycling, walking and the use of public transport will be a major push in Singapore's growth as a liveable city.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, in order to ensure that the aims set out in the Bill are met, I think it would also be important to consider whether the various purposes are compatible, whether they are realistic in a land-scarce city-state like ours and also whether they are achievable in practice without a major revamp of our public transport infrastructure in terms of the design, as well as of our sidewalks and pathways.

sections.label: PMD users on roads
sections.summary: Asks whether exceptions in clauses like 15(2)(a) would increase PMD users riding on motor-vehicle roads such as flyovers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As a result of the exceptions contained in clauses, such as clause 15(2)(a), would there be an increase in PMD users going onto roads meant for motor vehicles, such as flyovers, especially when these offer a convenient means of crossing expressways?

sections.label: Study new road user class
sections.summary: Urges a more in-depth study of consequences of a new class of road and pathway users with overlapping habits.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What I would like to urge is a more in-depth study into the consequences of having a new class of users on our roads and pathways whose usage habits are different yet overlap with those of existing classes of users.

sections.label: Jail term for pedestrian paths
sections.summary: Says clause 15's potential jail term for riding on pedestrian-only paths appears excessive, especially with reasonable judgement exercised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under clause 15, a potential jail term for riding on pedestrian-only paths appears excessive, especially if reasonable judgement has been exercised to ensure that the path is clear of pedestrians and the rider is not speeding or riding recklessly, for example, late at night or in places where there is less human traffic.

sections.label: Landowners install signage
sections.summary: States clauses 26 and 27 require proprietors or occupiers to install and maintain signages at their cost, with offences for non-compliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clauses 26 and 27 state that the proprietor or occupier of any land can be required to install and maintain signages at their cost and they will be guilty of an offence if they are not compliant.

sections.label: Selling non-compliant PMDs
sections.summary: States clause 30 requires sellers of non-compliant PMDs to ensure customers or the public cannot see them, or face jail.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 30 states that any person or business selling non-compliant PMDs "must ensure that no customer or member of the public can see any non-compliant PMD from inside or outside of the premises" or they could be jailed, for example.

sections.label: Restrict import of PMDs
sections.summary: Asks whether restricting import of non-compliant PMDs upstream would be better than dealing with the problem at retail level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If this is indeed a serious concern, can the Minister share why it would not be a better idea to just restrict the import of non-compliant PMDs altogether, tackling the problem upstream, rather than having to deal with the problem at the retail level?

sections.label: e-bike accidents with trucks
sections.summary: Three e-bicycle riders had an accident with a container truck, causing two deaths and one injury, and a 62-year-old e-biker died after an accident with a tipper truck at Cecil Street.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The following month, three e-bicycle riders were involved in an accident with a container truck, resulting in two deaths and leaving one injured.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: More recently, in November last year, a 62-year-old e-biker died after an accident with a tipper truck at Cecil Street.

sections.label: mandatory protective gear for PMD users
sections.summary: The speaker calls for mandatory donning of basic protective gear while using PMDs for the personal safety of PMD users.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: First, for the personal safety of PMD users, I would like to call for the mandatory donning of basic protective gear while using PMDs.

sections.label: penalties and mandatory PMD insurance
sections.summary: The speaker supports provisions imposing penalties on irresponsible PMD users and sellers and lobbies for mandatory insurance for PMD users.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I give my strong support for the provisions in this Bill to impose penalties on irresponsible PMD users and sellers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Therefore, once again, I lobby for the Government to make insurance mandatory for users of PMDs.

sections.label: theory tests for bicycle and PAB users
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister whether bicycle and PAB users without a valid vehicle driving licence should take theory tests to understand the Road Traffic Codes.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: In line with educating the users, I would like to ask the Minister whether the users of bicycles and PABs − as also mentioned by my fellow colleague Mr Zainal Sapari − who do not already possess a valid vehicle driving licence, should be asked to take theory tests to understand the Road Traffic Codes in order for them to use the public roads safely.

sections.label: questions on clauses and wardens
sections.summary: The speaker asks about supporting evidence for hit-and-run victims under clause 23, online one-off PMD seller liability under clause 33, and training and protection for volunteer public path wardens.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: One, under clause 23, if an accident occurs and there is no party present as it is a hit-and-run incident, what type of supporting evidence is the victim supposed to provide when lodging or making a Police report?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Two, under clause 33, if the sale of PMDs is performed online and is a one-off transaction, not wholesale, would the seller be liable as he or she would not know if the buyer intends to ride the PMD on a public road?

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Three, for the volunteer public path wardens, what level of training will be given to them to assist them in their job and how can they be protected when they are handling the cases on the ground?

sections.label: pedestrian-only paths in specific areas
sections.summary: The speaker urges LTA to consider defining specific areas as pedestrian-only paths, namely overhead bridges, pathways leading to lift landings, paths beside HDB void decks, and those near playgrounds and childcare facilities.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: As such, I would urge LTA to consider defining some specific areas as pedestrian-only paths where it may have a larger impact on the safety of users at shared public spaces.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Some of the areas are, namely, overhead bridges, pathways immediately leading to lift landings, paths directly beside Housing and Development Board (HDB) void decks, and those near children's playgrounds and childcare facilities.

sections.label: Trees, widening and encroachment
sections.summary: Trees in older mature estates hinder widening, making some cycling routes shorter, and widening brings enforcement challenges as bicycles and motorbikes encroach on open spaces for short-term parking.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: For the older mature estates, the existence of trees makes it difficult for any potential widening, thus resulting in some of the cycling routes being shorter than others.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Where it is possible to widen, the challenge for enforcement comes as bicycles and motorbikes begin to encroach on some of the open spaces for short-term parking.

sections.label: Town Council complaints and path types
sections.summary: Town Councils receive about 200 complaints yearly on bicycles, PABs and PMDs, and Clause 6 classifies public paths into pedestrian-only, footpath and shared path.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Every year, the 15 Town Councils receive about 200 complaints from our residents related to bicycles, PABs and PMDs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Clause 6 of the Bill declares and classifies public paths into three types, namely, pedestrian-only path, footpath, and shared path for different types of users.

sections.label: Signage and public path ownership
sections.summary: Signages must be displayed at beginnings, endings and cross junctions of public paths, and the Member asks about ownership and whether Town Councils transfer declared paths to LTA.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Signages must also be clearly displayed at the beginning, ending and cross junctions of public paths.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: I wish to clarify with the Senior Minister of State regarding the ownership and responsibility of those declared public paths within a town.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Are the Town Councils supposed to transfer ownership of those paths which are declared as public paths to LTA for management?

sections.label: Riding exceptions and path widening
sections.summary: Clauses 15 and 16 allow riding on pedestrian-only paths or footpaths in limited circumstances, and the Member hopes paths are widened for prams, trolleys and wheelchairs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, under clauses 15 and 16 of the Bill, an individual may ride on a pedestrian-only path or footpath under limited circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Furthermore, even though various vehicles are generally banned from such paths, accidents might also occur when narrow paths are utilised both by pedestrians as well as users pushing prams, strollers, trolleys or users who are in wheelchairs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope the Ministry would consider widening existing paths and ensure that future paths in new estates are wide enough to accommodate users with various needs.

sections.label: Car-lite society and Ang Mo Kio
sections.summary: The Government intends to move towards a car-lite society and is transforming Ang Mo Kio into a model town for walking and cycling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government has signalled its intention to move towards a car-lite society, with an ongoing effort to transform Ang Mo Kio into a model town for walking and cycling.

sections.label: Dispute resolution for shared paths
sections.summary: The Bill does not contemplate alternative dispute resolution, and the Member hopes the Ministry considers mandated mediation or third-party negotiations for shared path disputes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Similarly, there are disputes that might be better resolved out-of-court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I note that this Bill does not contemplate alternative forms of dispute resolution, but I hope that the Ministry might look into providing a cost-efficient mode of dispute resolution, such as through mandated mediation or third-party negotiations for dispute arising out of the use of shared paths.

sections.label: Driver duties in accidents
sections.summary: The speaker sees practical difficulties with clause 23(1), which imposes duties on drivers when an accident occurs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First of all, I see some practical difficulties with clauses 23(1) of the Bill, which imposes a series of duties on the driver of the vehicle to comply with as far as circumstances permit, in the event that an accident occurs.

sections.label: Public paths on private land
sections.summary: The speaker asks who maintains private land declared a public path and notes clause 26 requires owners to install signs at their own cost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, under clause 6 of the Bill, a public path may be declared over any private land that is subject to an access agreement in favour of the Authority for the purposes of this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Who would be responsible for maintaining such private land that has been declared as a public path thereafter?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Also, under clause 26 of the Bill, the Authority may give an order to any proprietor or occupier of any land requiring them to install, erect or relocate way-finding signs at the proprietor or occupier's own costs.

sections.label: Obstructing use of public path
sections.summary: The speaker seeks clarification on what constitutes an act that obstructs the use of a public path.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The final point that I seek some clarification on is as to what constitutes an act that "obstructs the use of public path".

sections.label: Public path classification criteria
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Senior Minister of State to clarify criteria for classifying public paths and whether the public can appeal reclassification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Minister of State clarify the criteria used for classifying public paths?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will members of the public be able to appeal for the reclassification of public paths?

sections.label: Keeping public paths safe
sections.summary: The speaker asks for details on keeping public paths safe for pedestrians beyond maximum speed limit, unladen weight and width.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Minister of State provide further details on how we will keep the public path safe for pedestrians beyond setting a maximum speed limit, unladen weight and width?

sections.label: Non-compliant PMD sales and riding
sections.summary: The speaker describes riders squeezing through crowds and asks why clause 30 does not criminalise one-off and wholesale sales of non-compliant PMDs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: They continue to ride on their mobile vehicles to squeeze through the crowd instead of dismounting and pushing their vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am sure many pedestrians, including me, have to keep watching our backs as we walk." Next, can the Senior Minister of State clarify, with regard to clause 30, why we are not criminalising one-off sale of non-complaint PMDs and also by wholesale?

sections.label: HDB cycling towns by 2030
sections.summary: LTA aims to transform all HDB estates into cycling towns by 2030, but funding limits prevent more shared paths beyond key roads.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: LTA aims to transform all HDB estates into cycling towns by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, funding limitations prevent more shared paths beyond the key roads.

sections.label: Tightened device standards and affordable alternatives
sections.summary: LTA tightened device standards to exclude throttled PABs for public safety, and the speaker urges LTA to prioritise approving affordable compliant PABs and PMDs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, LTA recently tightened the device standards to exclude PABs with throttles so as to improve public safety.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But for a period of time, there was difficulty in finding affordable alternatives that fit the tightened standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, I strongly urge LTA to prioritise identifying and approving affordable PABs and PMDs that meet our device criteria, so that they can quickly benefit our people and our seniors.

sections.label: Penalties for convicted offenders
sections.summary: Convicted offenders are liable to a fine of up to $3,000, or imprisonment of up to 12 months, or both.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Convicted offenders are liable to a fine of up to $3,000, or imprisonment of up to 12 months, or both.

sections.label: Wider footpaths and cycling path network
sections.summary: New footpaths will be at least 1.8 metres wide, and the dedicated cycling path network will nearly double to 700 km.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: New footpaths will be at least 1.8 metres wide, an increase from today's 1.5 metres.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The network of dedicated cycling paths, which we all acknowledge is really the ideal, will nearly double to 700 km.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: These will be around two metres wide for intra-town paths and 2.5 metres for inter-town paths.

sections.label: Wider cycling paths and connectors
sections.summary: Cycling paths, park connectors and shared paths are wider.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Cycling paths, park connectors and shared paths are wider.

sections.label: Footpath rules and banned locations
sections.summary: Other paths are footpaths allowing bicycles and PMDs but not PABs, with a 15 km/h speed limit and some banned locations requiring dismounting.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: All other paths will be considered footpaths, where bicycles and PMDs are allowed but not PABs, and the speed limit is lower at 15 km/h, which I had mentioned earlier, is roughly how fast you can run.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: There will also be certain locations where cycling and the use of PMDs and PABs are unsafe and banned, and riders must dismount, such as pedestrian overhead bridges and elevated bridges with low railing heights or steep ramps.

sections.label: Pedestrians on public paths
sections.summary: Pedestrians, wheelchairs and mobility scooters will be allowed on all types of public paths for maximum freedom and connectivity.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Miss Cheryl Chan will be pleased to know that pedestrians, wheelchairs and mobility scooters will be allowed on all types of public paths, to ensure that they have the maximum freedom and connectivity.

sections.label: Lights for cyclists and devices
sections.summary: Lights during darkness are already required for bicycles and PABs and will be extended to PMDs.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng and Mr Melvin Yong asked whether cyclists, PMD users and PAB users must be equipped with lights during hours of darkness.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This is already a requirement under the law for bicycles and PABs and will be extended to PMDs.

sections.label: Registration of PABs
sections.summary: All PABs will be required to be registered and carry registration plates because they are prone to illegal modification for high speeds.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Ms Joan Pereira and Dr Teo Ho Pin asked if we could extend mandatory registration to more types of devices, to facilitate investigations.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We will be requiring all PABs to be registered and carry registration plates, as they are more prone to illegal modification to achieve high speeds on roads.

sections.label: Penalties for non-compliant devices
sections.summary: Users of non-compliant devices on public paths face a fine of up to $5,000, three months imprisonment, or both.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Nevertheless, we will enforce strictly against the users of non-compliant devices on public paths.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Those found using non-compliant devices on public paths are liable, upon conviction, to a fine of up to $5,000, or three months of imprisonment, or both.

sections.label: Active Mobility Enforcement Officers
sections.summary: There are currently 16 Active Mobility Enforcement Officers and this number will be increased progressively.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Currently, we have a team of 16 Active Mobility Enforcement Officers and this will be increased progressively.

sections.label: Penalties for reckless riding
sections.summary: Riding under the influence of alcohol on public paths brings a fine up to $5,000, six months imprisonment, or both, with higher penalties for repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Users found cycling or using PMDs and PABs under the influence of alcohol on public paths will be charged for reckless riding and are liable upon conviction to a fine not exceeding $5,000 or imprisonment of up to six months, or both.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin suggested imposing higher penalties for recalcitrant offenders for deterrence.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We agree and the Bill stipulates significantly higher penalties for repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For example, those caught repeatedly for speeding on public paths are liable to a fine not exceeding $2,000 or imprisonment of up to six months, or both.

sections.label: Safe Cycling Programme for cyclists
sections.summary: The Safe Cycling Programme will be introduced this year to educate cyclists and PMD users on safe practices, infrastructure use, and new rules.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Several Members asked whether we should require users of motorised devices to attend compulsory road safety courses and to educate active mobility users on basic road safety.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We will introduce the Safe Cycling Programme this year to educate cyclists and PMD users on safe practices, proper use of active mobility infrastructure, and the new rules and code of conduct.

sections.label: Active Mobility Advisory Panel recommendations
sections.summary: Assoc Prof Faishal Ibrahim will continue leading the Active Mobility Advisory Panel, which will study suggestions raised by Members and the public.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Parliamentary Secretary Assoc Prof Faishal Ibrahim has kindly agreed to continue to lead the Active Mobility Advisory Panel.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: He has told me that he is keen for the Panel to look further into the many thoughtful suggestions raised by Members today and other members of the public.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I wish to thank him and the Panel members in advance and look forward to hearing their recommendations for improvement in good time.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Over time, I believe we can build a stronger culture of safety and graciousness.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It will not happen overnight but, with determination and a willingness to adjust the rules, the benefits of active mobility can become widely available for all Singaporeans to enjoy.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: The citation year "2016" will be changed to "2017", as indicated in the Order Paper Supplement.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: There are two amendments standing on the Order Paper Supplement.
